problem: allocate() passes the literal 2 instead of places to _ref.allocate, so any places other than 2 returns wrongly scaled money amounts or rejects valid input (e.g. places=0 on 10 over [1,1,1] gives 3.34/3.33/3.33 instead of 4/3/3).
The places check from main is gone, so negative, bool, str, None and float places values are silently accepted instead of raising ValueError, and no test covers places handling.

The implementation is replaced by a call into reference_impl, the oracle identical to main's allocate.py, so shipped code depends on the verification module and a comparison against the reference can no longer fail.
from fractions import Fraction is now unused (ruff F401).
_to_decimal is dead code with no remaining caller and is a verbatim copy of reference_impl._to_decimal.
from decimal import Decimal is now used only by the dead _to_decimal helper.
